crypto-lab-ablation-wire.note: Rust crypto core reviewed; WASM is built from that core

crypto-lab-biham-lens.note: Executes a toy SPN, not DES

crypto-lab-card-trick.note: Runs den Boer's physical-card AND protocol; no encryption

crypto-lab-context-ward.note: Python verifier uses the same SHA-256, HMAC and Ed25519 primitives already found in TS

crypto-lab-covert-channel-studio.note: Covert-channel encoders and detectors; no named cryptographic primitive implemented

crypto-lab-dp-noise.note: Runs discrete and continuous differential-privacy noise mechanisms

crypto-lab-export-grade.note: Runs TETRA TEA1 and a bounded state-recovery demonstration. Exhibits 5 and 6 add no cryptography: src/attack/rate.ts is arithmetic over the search Exhibit 3 already runs, and src/data/attacks.ts is a sourced citation table. AES-128/192/256 are named throughout that table and implemented nowhere in this lab.

crypto-lab-frost-threshold.note: Rust keygen, signing rounds and aggregation reviewed

crypto-lab-ghost-commit.note: WebCrypto hashes actual Git object preimages selected through a runtime algorithm map

crypto-lab-hqc-timing.note: Synthetic timing model; explicitly no HQC or BCH decoder

crypto-lab-hqc-timing-break.note: Runs a repetition-code surrogate and majority recovery; no HQC decoder

crypto-lab-iron-serpent.note: Argon2id is invoked through a bundled external WASM binary; its source is absent

crypto-lab-matsui-line.note: Executes a toy SPN for Matsui's linear attack

crypto-lab-model-breach.note: Executes a deliberately toy HiAE model, not the production cipher

crypto-lab-point-ledger.note: Fresh clone inspected; ECDSA is a data table and SHA-3 is merely the module path exporting SHAKE

crypto-lab-quantum-entropy.note: Runs both extractors on generated bits; source QRNG is modeled

crypto-lab-quantum-vault-kpqc.note: Rust and C source reviewed; three compiled WASM binaries remain opaque

crypto-lab-rsa-educational.note: Legacy Python RSA scripts inspected; browser lab implements RSA in JS

crypto-lab-shadow-vault.note: Rust crypto core reviewed; bundled WASM is built from that core

crypto-lab-silent-tally.note: Rust field arithmetic and Shamir share generation/reconstruction reviewed

crypto-lab-snark-arena.note: Checked-in circuit source and real snarkjs Groth16 flow reviewed; PLONK is shown only as a comparison

crypto-lab-syndrome-drain.note: Models decode-one-of-many work factors; no code-based KEM or decoder implemented

crypto-lab-syndrome-hints.note: Runs Prange-style and Stern information-set decoding against toy instances

crypto-lab-tc26-pair.note: C wrappers and TS calls reviewed; two compiled reference WASM binaries remain opaque

crypto-lab-timing-sidechannel.note: Runs early-exit comparison timing attack; no named cryptographic primitive

crypto-lab-token-tell.note: Python reference-data generators reviewed; browser uses TS detection and ECDSA

crypto-lab-pq-chooser.note: Derives every displayed public-key, ciphertext and signature size from real @noble/post-quantum output at page load rather than from constants; spec figures appear only as test oracles. Falcon ranges quoted in source are an offline 20,000-signature study, distinct from the live per-run range the table derives from FALCON_SAMPLES signatures. Classical baselines (X25519, ECDSA P-256, RSA-2048) are benchmarked by the same harness; RSA keygen is reported not-measured by design.

crypto-lab-sm9-forge.note: Implements the SM9 family in src/sm9/ — extraction for both master key pairs, signature, key exchange, KEM and public key encryption — over the BN256 curve and R-ate pairing, checked against the worked examples in the standard's annexes. SM3 and SM4 are imported, not implemented here. Boneh-Franklin IBE is drawn as the contrast to SM9's inversion, never computed. The comparison oracle is vendored GmSSL-JS, which is opaque to the scanner.
